messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I got two QTL from scanone, them when I did scantwo, I got an additional qtl, and they all look like real QTL (the one one chr3 was not detected before). What can possibly cause this, should I trust the stepwise qtl results?
Thank you!

5...@56.9  1     0.03160 4.448  9.605   21.25            0  7.97e-06 ***

When I only selected one of them, plus the one consistently identified from both scanone and stepwise qtl, and redo the fitqtl, the new one became  not significant. Then I just chose the ONE QTL modle with the QTL that could be consistently detected, and use addqtl, I didn't find any new QTL, including the two closely linked QTL identified from the stepwiseqtl . Should I only choose the one QTL model then?

messages.subject: singular matrix error for mqmscan
messages.subject_clean: singular matrix error for mqmscan
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I am trying to do mqmscan with my RIL data, 7LGs, ~6,000 markers. According to the tutorial there are two approaches to fill in the missing data :1) mqmaugmentdata or 2) fill.geno. The first approach took super long (running on a cluster for >3 days and still not showing any results and is still running). The fill.geno only took a few seconds but when I proceed with the mqmscan, I got an error message and the calculation was stopped:

FATALError in mqmscan(AE, model = "dominance", pheno.col = "rep1") :

 Singular matrix

Calls: mqmscan -> .C
Execution halted
Could anybody provide any suggestions as what should be done? My one way scan and two way scan was fine.
Thank you

messages.subject: "logical subscript too long" when running permutations
messages.subject_clean: "logical subscript too long" when running permutations
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'm trying to run scanone permutations for several phenotypes.  This code works fine on my mac, but not on our linux server and I can't figure out why or exactly what this error is.  I tried to create a reproducible example, but neither hyper or listeria have multiple numerical phenotypes to test this with.  Any ideas or suggestions?

Thanks!

For various reasons we have an older version of R (3.0.2) and Rqtl (1.33-7) on both systems.

on the mac, runs fine:

> # calculate permutations
> perms = 10
> method = "hk"
> nodes = 1
>
> # get a list of phenotypes..
> phenos = as.data.frame(colnames(cross$pheno), stringsAsFactors=F)

> # don't include ID column..
> phenos = phenos[-1,]
>
> ptm <- proc.time()
> earlyqtlpermsscan1 = scanone(cross, pheno.col=phenos[1:2], method=method, n.perm=perms, n.cluster=nodes, addcovar=NULL, verbose=T)
Permutation 1
Permutation 2
Permutation 3
Permutation 4
Permutation 5
Permutation 6
Permutation 7
Permutation 8
Permutation 9
Permutation 10
> proc.time() - ptm
   user  system elapsed
  6.067   2.563   8.651

    but on the server:

> ptm <- proc.time()
> earlyqtlpermsscan1 = scanone(cross, pheno.col=phenos[1:2], method=method, n.perm=perms, n.cluster=nodes, addcovar=NULL, verbose=T)
Permutation 1
Permutation 2
Permutation 3
Permutation 4
Permutation 5
Permutation 6
Permutation 7
Permutation 8
Permutation 9
Permutation 10
> proc.time() - ptm
   user  system elapsed
  7.732   0.321   8.045
<simpleError in unclass(x)[repl, lodcolumn, drop = FALSE]: (subscript) logical subscript too long>

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] R/qtl unable to provide summary results.
messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] R/qtl unable to provide summary results.
messages.body_plain:
R/qtl is capable of handling 4510 markers and 180 individuals.

Separately, you wrote with the following information on your session:

> library(qtl)
> HW=read.cross("csv",file="HW.csv",na.strings="-")
 --Read the following data:
  180  individuals
  4510 markers
  1  phenotypes
 --Estimating genetic map
data(HW)
summary(HW)

This indicates that R is in the processing of estimating the genetic map among markers: the last line said "--Estimating genetic map". Also the ">" symbol is the R "prompt". It shows up with R is ready to accept input. It hadn't appeared yet, because R is still working on the map.

If your CSV file doesn't contain marker locations, they will be estimated, but this can take a *really* long time (depending on the nature of the data).

Try read.cross again with the argument estimate.map=FALSE

  HW <- read.cross("csv", file="HW.csv", na.strings="-", estimate.map=FALSE)

If you use estimate.map=FALSE, read.cross will insert an arbitrary set of positions for the markers.

karl

Additionally, I tried running the fitqtl just to see what would happen and got an error (Error in solve.default(t(Z) %*% Z, t(Z) %*% X) : system is computationally singular: reciprocal condition number = 1.49755e-24).

Any thoughts about what is going on?

I will note that I am trying to run a covariate with my analysis. I created: head.covar <- pull.pheno(sawfly.cross, pheno.col=19) and used addcovar=head.covar when running my permutations. However, when I tried to use that same code in my stepwise qtl, I had to adjust it to covar=sawfly.cross$pheno$Head.Area because I got an error saying it had an incorrect number of dimensions. I don't know if this is related to my problem.

Thank you,
Claire

messages.subject_clean: genetic map construction with BCsFt
messages.body_plain:
Dear Karl Broman, dear R/qtl users

I recently started working on GBS data and would like to construct a genetic map from an F7 population and a F2 population of 3 species (F7: species1 x species2  ;  F2: species1 x species3).
As i have a draft genome of species1, i used it to construct the markers.

I am using the 'Genetic map consturciton with R/qtl'-script, which is very helpful.
Still i have some general questions about how to start the genetic map as which markers to include for the inital building of a map.
Should i be very stringent for the markers to fit the expected allel frequencies (chisquare-test)? Can i include markers with missing data?
If i allow for no missing-data markers, about 50 % of the markers collaps if i remove duplicates, meaning they are clustering together w/o recombination events.

Because i think that valuable markers (showing recombination) would be missed for the genetic map building,
i started including also markers with up to 20 % of missing data into the inital map building.

Could you tell me what decisions one should make when creating a genetic map from scratch and which markers to include?

As the default setting in R/qtl is an F2 cross, i expect no problems in generating the map for the F2 population.
After creating the assumed number of linkage groups with fromLinkageGroups(), I first applied the orderMarkers() function and afterwards started to switch markers manually, if they looked odd in the RF plot.

Whereas for the F7, i used the option in read.cross() F.gen=7.
I ran the est.map() function and got an inital map.
Now i would like to order the markers as i did with the F2 population using first automatic ordering and do manual ordering afterwards.
But i ran into following error:

RIL7lg <- orderMarkers(RIL7lg, chr = 7, use.ripple = FALSE, map.function = "haldane", verbose = TRUE)
Error in countXO(cross, 1) : ripple not available for cross bcsft

Is there another way to create a first automatic ordering of the markers in a chromosome?

Also the function plotGeno seems not to be working for bcsft-crosses.

plotGeno(RIL7lg)
Error in locateXO(cross) :
  locateXO only working for backcross, intercross or RI strains.
In addition: Warning message:
In plotGeno(RIL7lg) : First running calc.errorlod.

Thank you very much,

Michel

is a bug that is revealed by the problem of having multiple QTL at very close to the same position, and this seems to arise because you have very strong QTL effects, and Haley-Knott regression isn't working well in this case.

I'd recommend switching to the multiple imputation method (method="imp"): use sim.geno in place of calc.genoprob, and method="imp" in place of method="hk".

karl
